title: Platform team wiki: systems & services playbook, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This page is the canonical Platform team playbook for systems & services, dashboards and alerts, runbooks, retrospectives, and the Q2 2026 roadmap. It consolidates operational expectations, ownership, and step-by-step how-tos for common platform tasks. Use this as the starting point for incident response, regular on-call work, and quarterly planning.

1) Purpose and scope
- Audience: platform engineers, SREs, product engineers integrating platform services, and support responders.
- Scope: core platform services (control-plane-api, request-router, batch-ingestor, kv-cache, telemetry-pipeline), dashboards maintained by Platform, alerting policy, major runbooks, and roadmap items owned by Platform Systems & Services.

2) Ownership and contact points
- Platform systems & services team leads: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com), Diego Ramos (diego@redwood.com).
- On-call rotations: platform-oncall@redwood.com (primary), platform-esc@redwood.com (secondary).
- PagerDuty service: PD:platform-prod. Slack channel: #platform-prod (monitored 24x7 by on-call).

3) Systems & services inventory (high-level)
Service | Purpose | Owner | Critical SLOs
- control-plane-api | API for model routing, tokenization orchestration | owner: control-plane@redwood.com | API latency p95 < 120ms, availability 99.95% monthly
- request-router | Smart routing and fallback policies | owner: routing@redwood.com | request success rate > 99.9% (5m), tail latency p99 < 500ms
- kv-cache | Prefix caching layer for KV lookups | owner: caching@redwood.com | cache hit rate >= 85% for steady-state workloads
- telemetry-pipeline | Ingest and process traces/metrics/logs | owner: telemetry@redwood.com | processing lag < 30s, data loss < 0.01%
- batch-ingestor | Batch job runner for offline jobs and model evals | owner: batch@redwood.com | job success rate > 98% monthly

4) Dashboards and observability (what to use when)
Overview: Platform dashboards are the single source of truth for operational health. Dashboards are in Grafana under the "Platform" folder. Panel IDs and owners are listed below.

Critical dashboards (examples):
- PLAT:ControlPlane-Overview (dashboard/PLAT-CTRL-001) — Owner: control-plane@redwood.com. Shows API latency (p50/p95/p99), QPS, error rates, and deployment versions.
- PLAT:Routing-Health (dashboard/PLAT-ROUTE-001) — Owner: routing@redwood.com. Shows queue depth, routing fallbacks, and model variant churn.
- PLAT:KvCache-Metrics (dashboard/PLAT-CACHE-001) — Owner: caching@redwood.com. Cache hit rate, eviction rate, memory usage by shard.
- PLAT:Telemetry-Pipeline (dashboard/PLAT-TEL-001) — Owner: telemetry@redwood.com. Ingest lag, DLQ counts, consumer lag (Kafka).

Dashboard best practices:
- Always open the service overview first (p95 latency, error rate, capacity).
- Check recent deploys: deployments panel correlates errors with version rollouts.
- Use the timeshift comparison (last 1h vs last 24h) to detect regressions.

5) Alerting policy (thresholds and runbook mapping)
High-level rules:
- Severity P0 (page): Service unavailable or customer-facing outage impacting >5% of requests or SLO breach with immediate customer impact. Notify PD:platform-prod, escalate to on-call manager.
- Severity P1 (page + email): Elevated error rate or latency likely to cause SLO breach within 30 minutes (e.g., error rate >0.5% sustained for 5m, p95 latency > 200ms for control-plane-api for 5m).
- Severity P2 (email + slack): Degradation that does not immediately threaten SLOs.

Common alert examples and thresholds:
- control-plane-api: error_rate_5m > 0.5% (trigger P1).
- control-plane-api: p95_latency_5m > 200ms and p99_latency_5m > 600ms (trigger P1).
- request-router: routing-fallback-rate_5m > 1% (trigger P1).
- kv-cache: cache_hit_rate_5m < 70% (trigger P2).
- telemetry-pipeline: consumer_lag > 50,000 messages or processing_lag > 120s (trigger P1).

Alert-to-runbook mapping (quick reference):
- control-plane-api alerts -> Runbook: control-plane-api-incident
- request-router alerts -> Runbook: request-router-fallbacks
- kv-cache alerts -> Runbook: kv-cache-degradation
- telemetry-pipeline alerts -> Runbook: telemetry-pipeline-lag

6) Runbooks (templates and key playbooks)
Structure for every runbook:
- Title, Owner, PagerDuty service, Slack channel, Severity mapping, Quick checks, Escalation path, Mitigation steps, Postmortem checklist.

Runbook: control-plane-api-incident (summary)
- Quick checks: confirm alert in Grafana and PD. Check recent deploys in deployments panel and GitHub release tags.
- Step 1: Determine scope: run query for 1m, 5m error rate and top-5 error codes.
- Step 2: If error spike correlates with a deployment, roll back to previous stable tag (CI job: platform/rollbacks -> run: ./scripts/rollback.sh --service control-plane-api --to <tag>). Notify release engineer.
- Step 3: If no recent deploy, inspect upstream dependencies (auth, model-serving endpoints) and circuit-breakers. Increase logging level for problematic endpoints.
- Step 4: If still degraded after 15 minutes, trigger capacity scale (playbook automation: kubectl scale deployment control-plane-api --replicas N) and trigger global routing fallback to dedicated model-variants.
- Post-incident: start postmortem within 48 hours, link to incident ticket, assign action owners, add to weekly retro if severity P0/P1.

Runbook: kv-cache-degradation (summary)
- Quick checks: cache hit rate panel, eviction rate, memory pressure per shard.
- Steps: identify hot keys, increase cache shard count (k8s config), temporarily enable model-side prefix caching bypass to reduce pressure, schedule offline rewarm job.

7) How-tos (common operational tasks)
How-to: deploy a config change to dashboards/alerts
1. Create PR in infra/observability-configs repo with dashboard JSON or alert rule change.
2. Add owner as reviewer and include test panel screenshots.
3. CI will validate JSON schema and run smoke test (grafana-api dry-run).
4. Merge, then run ./scripts/grafana-deploy --env prod --dashboard <id>. Monitor panels for 10 minutes for unexpected spikes.

How-to: add a new service to Platform inventory
1. Create a new page in the team wiki under /services/<service-name> with owner, SLOs, deploy steps, runbook link, and dashboard IDs.
2. Add the service to the Platform service registry (internal catalog): POST /internal-catalog/services with metadata.
3. Create Grafana dashboard stub (use dashboard template DOCS) and alert rules.
4. Schedule a short runthrough in weekly on-call handover meeting.

8) Incident retrospectives (recent learnings, Q1 2026)
Summary of top incidents:
- Incident 2026-01-18 (control-plane-api degradation): Root cause — bad rollout of connection pooling change. Mitigation — improved canary policy, automated pre-deploy perf checks. Action items: add pre-deploy synthetic load test (owner: Diego Ramos, due 2026-04-01).
- Incident 2026-02-06 (telemetry pipeline lag): Root cause — consumer config drift after broker upgrade. Mitigation — enforce consumer config checks in CI and alert on lag > 30s. Action items: implement CI config schema enforcement (owner: Priya Singh, due 2026-03-15).

Retrospective themes:
- Improve pre-deploy canaries and perf gating for high-traffic services.
- Stronger config CI validation for observability and Kafka consumers.
- Better runbook run-throughs during on-call handovers.

9) Roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities and milestones)
- Q2 2026 Goal: Increase platform SLO headroom and reduce incident MTTR by 30%.
Planned work:
- Q2 Week 1-4: Implement pre-deploy synthetic perf tests for control-plane-api (owner: Diego Ramos).
- Q2 Week 3-8: Telemetry pipeline reliability improvements (consumer config enforcement, DLQ alerting) (owner: Priya Singh).
- Q2 Week 6-12: Unified dashboard templates and alert-rule library, publish standard alert severities (owner: observability@redwood.com).
- Q2 Week 8-16: Automated rollback tooling enhancements and canary auto-abort for SLA regressions (owner: platform-safety@redwood.com).

10) Team wiki hygiene and conventions
- Page naming: lower-case, dash-separated, include year when appropriate (e.g., control-plane-api-runbook-2026).
- All runbooks must be reviewed quarterly by the owner and re-signed in the page header.
- When adding new labels/tags, prefer standard set: platform, runbook, oncall, alert, dashboard.
- Use the checklist template for runbooks (see appendix).

11) Appendices
Appendix A — Runbook template checklist:
- Title, Owner, PagerDuty, Slack channel, Severity mapping, Quick checks, Escalation path, Mitigation, Rollback steps, Contact list, Postmortem link.

Appendix B — Useful CLI snippets
- Rollback example: ./scripts/rollback.sh --service control-plane-api --to v1.12.3
- Scale deployment: kubectl scale deployment control-plane-api --replicas 12 -n platform-prod
- Grafana deploy dry-run: ./scripts/grafana-deploy --dry-run --dashboard dashboard/PLAT-CTRL-001

Appendix C — References and related pages
- Platform playbook (detailed): /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-2026.json
- Dashboards and alert rules repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-observability-configs.git

If you are on-call: follow the "Quick incident checklist" pinned at the top of this page, and escalate to the on-call manager if mitigation steps do not restore SLOs within 30 minutes.
